_comment: Output schema for parser.py / parse_jd(). Fields added to job dict under job['parsed']. Source: PARSER_PROMPT in prompts/parser-prompt.md. v1.5: truly_required + preferred_skills (renamed from must_have_skills/nice_to_have_skills); added role_in_plain_english, company_context, verbatim_for_cv.
truly_required: ONLY specific technical skills where JD uses 'must', 'required', 'minimum', or 'essential'. No years of experience, degrees, or soft skills.
preferred_skills: specific technical skills where JD uses 'preferred', 'ideally', 'bonus', 'nice to have', or 'plus' (same technical-only rule)
technical_stack: all specific technologies, tools, platforms mentioned anywhere in the JD
experience_requirements: years of experience, domain background, education/degree, soft skills, and competency requirements
role_in_plain_english: 2-3 sentences describing day-to-day work in plain language. No jargon.

what_they_value: 2-3 inferred real values from JD language

verbatim_for_cv: 5-8 exact domain-specific phrases from JD a CV should mirror. Each 2-6 words.
responsibilities_summary: 2-3 sentence summary of what the role does
team_size_hints: any mentions of team size or reports, or null
salary_mentioned: any salary info found as string, or null
remote_restriction: geographic restriction for remote jobs (e.g. 'US only', 'North America', 'EMEA') or null if unrestricted/not applicable
red_flags: anything concerning: unrealistic requirements, too many hats, etc.
key_phrases: 3-5 distinctive phrases that capture what makes this role unique
